ideas.title: HHS opens the door to unapproved 'wellness peptides': what's now for sale, what 'unapproved' means, and what we don't know about self-injecting them
ideas.angle: A consumer-safety explainer with tension. Federal health officials just loosened access to compounds the FDA never approved, and peptide culture overlaps with GLP-1 and biohacking audiences. The piece separates unverified manufacturing and dosing from proven harm and asks who carries the risk now.
ideas.why_now: Policy announced 10/28. A rising search query asks almost exactly this question, and consumers have no authoritative answer yet.
ideas.is_it_real: The policy is reported by Reuters and ABC News, so the news peg is solid. Specifics are not confirmed yet: which peptides are covered, the 'temporary' terms, and how compliance works. These must be checked against the FDA/HHS notice before any claim is made. Don't frame 'unapproved' as meaning either 'dangerous' or 'safe'.
